--- title: "[GAMClassifier]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Scikit-learn compatible GAM classifier (binary). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/sklearn.py#L261-L435){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GAMClassifier(formula=None, *, method="GCV", select=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `GAMClassifier` wraps `whittaker.gam.GAM` behind the scikit-learn `BaseEstimator` / `ClassifierMixin` interface for binary classification. It always fits a `whittaker.families.binomial.Binomial(link="logit")` family internally — i.e. a logistic GAM — so the linear predictor is related to the class-1 probability `\mu` by the logit link, `\eta = \log(\mu / (1 - \mu))`. Only two-class problems are supported: `fit()` raises a `ValueError` if `y` does not contain exactly two distinct labels. The formula-building behavior (synthetic feature names, default `s(xi)`-per-feature formula, or an explicit `formula`) is identical to `GAMRegressor`; see that class for details. Fitted attributes follow the scikit-learn classifier convention: `self.classes_` holds the two observed labels sorted ascending (as returned by `numpy.unique`), and `predict_proba` returns probability columns ordered to match `self.classes_` (column 0 is `P(y = classes_[0])`, column 1 is `P(y = classes_[1])`). This makes `GAMClassifier` compatible with `Pipeline`, `GridSearchCV`/`RandomizedSearchCV` (scored via `"accuracy"`, `"roc_auc"`, or a custom scorer), and any tooling that consumes `predict_proba`, such as `sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV` or manual decision-threshold tuning on the predicted probabilities. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : GAM formula for the right-hand side (e.g. `"s(x0) + s(x1)"`), or a complete formula containing `"~"`. If it contains `"~"` it is used verbatim; otherwise the response `"y"` is prepended. If `None` (the default), a formula with one `s(xi)` smooth per input feature is generated automatically. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["GCV"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing parameter selection criterion forwarded to `GAM.fit`: `"GCV"` (default), `"REML"`, or `"ML"`. See `whittaker.gam.GAM.fit` for the meaning of each option. [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, enable double-penalty smooth selection, forwarded to `GAM.fit`. Defaults to `False`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} As with `GAMRegressor`, the hyperparameters exposed to `GridSearchCV`/`RandomizedSearchCV` via `get_params()` are the constructor arguments — `formula`, `method`, and `select` — since scikit-learn's `get_params` introspects `__init__`. There is no `family` parameter here because the family is fixed to `Binomial(link="logit")`. The smoothing parameters `\lambda_j` are always selected internally by `method` during `fit()` rather than being directly tunable. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#778fa5b8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.sklearn import GAMClassifier rng = np.random.default_rng(0) X = rng.uniform(-2, 2, size=(300, 2)) logit = 1.5 * np.sin(X[:, 0]) - X[:, 1] p = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit)) y = rng.binomial(1, p) clf = GAMClassifier(formula="s(x0) + s(x1)") clf.fit(X, y) clf.predict_proba(X[:5]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` array([[0.13026716, 0.86973284], [0.74973502, 0.25026498], [0.57189211, 0.42810789], [0.46846977, 0.53153023], [0.82997728, 0.17002272]]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#fadd5540 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} clf.predict(X[:5]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` array([1, 0, 0, 1, 0]) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the GAM classifier.
predict() Predict class labels for X.
predict_proba() Predict class probabilities for X.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the GAM classifier. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/sklearn.py#L339-L386){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(X, y, **fit_params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Validates `X` and `y` with `check_X_y`, records the two observed class labels in `self.classes_`, assigns synthetic feature names, builds the model formula, and fits an internal `Binomial(link="logit")` `whittaker.gam.GAM` to the resulting data dictionary using `method` and `select`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [X]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Feature matrix, shape `(n_samples, n_features)`. Coerced to `float64` and validated by `sklearn.utils.validation.check_X_y`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Class labels, shape `(n_samples,)`. Must contain exactly two distinct values (e.g. `0`/`1`, or any two comparable labels); coerced to `float64` alongside `X`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [GAMClassifier]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self`, with fitted attributes `classes_` (the two sorted class labels seen in `y`), `n_features_in_`, `feature_names_`, and `gam_` (the underlying fitted `Binomial`-family `whittaker.gam.GAM`). ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `y` contains fewer or more than two distinct values, since `GAMClassifier` supports binary classification only. ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict class labels for X. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/sklearn.py#L417-L435){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(X) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Calls `predict_proba()` and, for each sample, returns the label in `self.classes_` corresponding to the higher predicted probability (i.e. thresholding at `0.5` on the positive-class probability). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [X]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Feature matrix, shape `(n_samples, n_features_in_)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Predicted class labels, shape `(n_samples,)`, drawn from `self.classes_`. ::: ### [predict_proba()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict class probabilities for X. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-psis-loo/whittaker/sklearn.py#L388-L415){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_proba(X) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Requires `fit()` to have been called first. Converts `X` into the internal data dictionary and calls the fitted `Binomial`-family `GAM`'s `predict()` to obtain the probability of the positive class (`self.classes_[1]`), then derives the probability of the negative class as its complement. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [X]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Feature matrix, shape `(n_samples, n_features_in_)`. Coerced to `float64` and validated by `sklearn.utils.validation.check_array`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Predicted probabilities, shape `(n_samples, 2)`. Column `0` is `P(y == self.classes_[0])` and column `1` is `P(y == self.classes_[1])`, matching the scikit-learn convention that `predict_proba` columns are ordered by `self.classes_`. :::
